record.original_question: If f : {-1,1}^n -> {-1,1} is monotone, must its total influence satisfy I[f] < o(sens[f])?

evidence.quote: Statement: Let f : {-1, 1}^n -> {-1, 1} be monotone. Then I[ f ] < o(sens[ f ]).

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $f:\{-1,1\}^n\to\{-1,1\}$ be a monotone Boolean function (i.e., $f(x)\le f(y)$ whenever $x\le y$ coordinatewise under the order $-1<1$). For $x\in\{-1,1\}^n$, define the local sensitivity
$$s(f,x)=\bigl|\{i\in[n]:f(x)\ne f(x^{\oplus i})\}\bigr|,$$
where $x^{\oplus i}$ denotes $x$ with its $i$-th coordinate flipped. Define the maximum sensitivity
$$\mathrm{sens}(f)=\max_{x\in\{-1,1\}^n} s(f,x),$$
and the total influence (equivalently, average sensitivity)
$$I[f]=\mathbb{E}_{x}\bigl[s(f,x)\bigr]=\sum_{i=1}^n \Pr_x\bigl[f(x)\ne f(x^{\oplus i})\bigr].$$
It is well known that $I[f]\le \mathrm{sens}(f)$ for every monotone $f$. Question: must every monotone $f:\{-1,1\}^n\to\{-1,1\}$ satisfy
$$I[f] = o\bigl(\mathrm{sens}(f)\bigr)$$
as $n\to\infty$? Equivalently, is it the case that for every $c>0$ there exist no infinite family of monotone functions with $I[f]\ge c\cdot \mathrm{sens}(f)$?
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is closely tied to a conjecture of Servedio comparing average and maximum sensitivity of monotone Boolean functions. The best known upper bound is $I[f]\le \ln(2)\cdot \mathrm{sens}(f)(1+o(1))$, which does not establish $I[f]=o(\mathrm{sens}(f))$. On the other side, O'Donnell–Servedio constructed monotone functions with $I[f]=\Omega(\mathrm{sens}(f)^{0.61})$, and subsequent work (e.g., on $k$-CNFs) has further narrowed the gap, but no construction is known that refutes $I[f]=o(\mathrm{sens}(f))$. The question therefore appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: On the Average Sensitivity and Density of k-CNF Formulas
status_evidence.snippet: yields the largest known separation between the average and maximum sensitivity of monotone Boolean functions, making progress on a conjecture of Servedio
status_evidence.claim: Progress, not resolution, on Servedio's conjecture about average vs maximum sensitivity of monotone functions.

status_evidence.title: Computational Applications of Noise Sensitivity (O'Donnell thesis)
status_evidence.snippet: existence of a monotone function F with AS(F) = Omega(S(F)^0.61)
status_evidence.claim: Lower-bound construction showing average sensitivity can be a non-trivial polynomial in the maximum sensitivity for monotone functions.
